Fantasy.style_rules: Vivid world-building. Magic has rules and costs. Sensory-rich descriptions. Formal or archaic dialogue for high fantasy; modern for urban. Avoid anachronistic language in historical fantasy. Show magic through consequences, not exposition.

Science Fiction.style_rules: Ground speculation in plausible science. Technical vocabulary when appropriate but explain through context. Sense of wonder and scale. Avoid info-dumps; reveal world through character experience. Tension between technology and humanity.

Mystery.style_rules: Plant clues fairly. Red herrings should be plausible. Pacing: steady revelation. Avoid revealing the solution too early. Dialogue should carry subtext. End chapters on questions or discoveries.

Thriller.style_rules: Short sentences. Fast pacing. High stakes. Cliffhanger chapter endings. Tension through uncertainty. Avoid lengthy exposition. Show danger through physical sensation.

Horror.style_rules: Build dread through atmosphere, not gore (unless splatterpunk). Short sentences increase tension. Sensory details: sounds, smells, temperature. Avoid over-explaining the threat. Leave ambiguity. Fear lives in what's unseen.

Romance.style_rules: Emotional interiority is central. Dialogue carries subtext. Tension through obstacles and misunderstandings. Physical descriptions through desire. Avoid purple prose. Show attraction through behavior, not just statement.

Historical Fiction.style_rules: Period-accurate vocabulary and social norms. Avoid anachronisms. Show daily life through sensory detail. Dialogue reflects class and era. Research-backed but never info-dumpy. Characters should feel of their time, not modern minds in costumes.

Crime / Detective.style_rules: Procedural detail grounds the story. Moral ambiguity is key. Show the cost of crime. Dialogue is terse, cynical, layered. Avoid glorifying violence. Pacing alternates between action and investigation.

Adventure.style_rules: Physical sensation dominates: exhaustion, hunger, weather. Short sentences in action. Pacing alternates between tension and recovery. Show the environment as an antagonist. Characters revealed through choices under pressure.

Literary Fiction.style_rules: Prose quality is the point. Interiority, subtext, thematic depth. Slower pacing. Every sentence earns its place. Avoid genre cliches. Show character through small moments. Ambiguity is acceptable.

Young Adult (YA).style_rules: First-person or close third. Immediate, present-tense energy. Protagonist is teen (13-18). Voice is authentic to age. Themes: identity, belonging, first love, rebellion. Avoid condescension. Pacing is faster than adult fiction.

Middle Grade.style_rules: Ages 8-12. Clear moral framework. Humor is important. Shorter chapters. Protagonist solves problems. Avoid graphic content. Hopeful tone. Adult characters are secondary.

Comedy / Humor.style_rules: Timing is everything. Setup and payoff. Exaggeration with a straight face. Dialogue should be witty, not forced. Avoid explaining the joke. Physical comedy through precise description.

Western.style_rules: Sparse, laconic prose. Landscape as character. Moral ambiguity. Violence has weight. Dialogue is clipped, minimal. Show the cost of the frontier. Avoid romanticizing.

War / Military.style_rules: Procedural accuracy (weapons, tactics, ranks). Show the human cost. Avoid glorification. Dialogue is clipped, professional. Sensory: noise, smoke, mud, fear. Alternating between action and quiet moments.

Speculative / Weird.style_rules: Defamiliarize the ordinary. Unsettling, not scary. Blend genres freely. Dream-logic is acceptable. Avoid explaining the weirdness. Let the reader sit with discomfort.

Superhero.style_rules: Balance spectacle with character. Powers have costs. Moral complexity. Action scenes need clarity. Avoid excessive origin stories. Show the civilian life alongside the hero life.

Epistolary.style_rules: Voice varies by correspondent. Show, don't tell through documents. Gaps in the record create mystery. Each document must advance plot or character. Avoid info-dumps in letters.

Drama.style_rules: Character-driven. Conflict from relationships, not action. Dialogue is the primary tool. Subtext and silence matter. Slow burn. Show the cracks before the break.

Sports.style_rules: Physical sensation of the sport. Show the body under stress. Team dynamics as metaphor for life. Avoid play-by-play narration. The sport is the vehicle, character is the story.

Southern Gothic.style_rules: Decay, grotesque, heat, family curses. Atmosphere over plot. Characters are flawed, often grotesque. Landscape reflects moral decay. Slow, oppressive pacing.

Magical Realism.style_rules: Magic is mundane, accepted, unexplained. No wonder, no fear. Grounded in reality with one impossible element. Lyrical prose. The magic serves the theme, not the plot.

Noir.style_rules: First-person or close third. Cynical, world-weary voice. Short, punchy sentences. Rain, neon, shadows. Moral ambiguity. Everyone is corrupt. The city is a character.

Dystopian.style_rules: Show the oppression through daily life, not speeches. The system is the antagonist. Protagonist discovers the truth gradually. Avoid heavy-handed politics. Ground in sensory detail.

Utopian.style_rules: Explore the cost of perfection. Conflict comes from within the system. Avoid naivety. The utopia should feel real and appealing before revealing its flaws.

Slice of Life.style_rules: No plot required. Character and moment are the story. Quiet, observational. Find the extraordinary in the ordinary. Avoid manufactured conflict.

Fan Fiction.style_rules: Respect source material voice. Add depth to existing characters. AU changes one variable and explores consequences. Avoid Mary Sue. Know the canon deeply.

Metafiction.style_rules: The narrative acknowledges itself. Playful, ironic. Risk of pretension. Must serve a purpose beyond cleverness. Reader awareness is the point.

Flash Fiction.style_rules: Every word counts. One moment, one image, one emotion. No setup, no resolution. End on resonance, not conclusion.

Serial / Web Fiction.style_rules: Regular update rhythm. Each chapter must satisfy AND hook. Power progression must feel earned. Cliffhangers are essential. Community feedback may influence direction.
